name: Rosewood Kauri Cliffs
positioning: Golf lodge on a 6,000-acre coastal property in Northland, New Zealand, with a par 72 championship course above the Pacific
best_for: Golfers who want a championship course running to clifftops above the Pacific
Families or groups wanting a private villa with its own pool

facts.text: Rosewood Kauri Cliffs is in Northland, New Zealand.
The property covers 6,000 coastal acres, which guests can explore on an ATV tour.
The par 72 championship golf course was designed by David Harman.
The Spa is set in native bush and has a sauna, jacuzzi and heated pool.
The Dining Room's menu highlights local seasonal produce and changes daily.
The Dining Room serves breakfast and dinner from an a la carte menu.
A food truck at the 19th Tee serves lunch overlooking the Pacific and is open seasonally.
Private dining settings include the Villas and the Green Room.
Grand Ocean View Junior Suites have a large private balcony overlooking the golf course.
The Four-Bedroom Villa sits in its own private enclave with a fireplace, kitchen and saltwater swimming pool.
Scenic helicopter tours fly over the Bay of Islands.
Stargazing is offered as a guided night walk through the forest.

highlights.text: The 18-hole championship course runs across farmland to the edge of cliffs high above the Pacific Ocean.
Tide to Table Dining is a private dining experience on Pink Beach.
The Taipa Salt Pig salt is handmade on the property's Pink Beach.
The Two Bedroom Villa has a terrace with a private infinity pool and jacuzzi.
Julian Robertson built the golf retreat on a 6,000-acre working sheep farm.

considerations.text: The nearest outside dining is a 30-minute drive away in Kerikeri.
There is a jacket rule at dinner.
WhataHotel notes the remote location requires a scenic but lengthy drive from major airports.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: The Lodge at Kauri Cliffs
